title: Almost all 180 neurons can be unmatched in maximum matchings of two selected adult worm chemical graphs
abstract: We tested whether a small matching deficit identifies a small set of possible unmatched neurons in two adult worm wiring maps. Directed chemical graphs on 180 common neurons had maximum matching sizes of 159 and 160. They left 21 and 20 targets unmatched per maximum matching. Yet all 180 neurons in adult 7 and 179 in adult 8 could be unmatched in at least one maximum matching. Removing edges with fewer than three synapses gave possible sets of 81 and 56 neurons, with Jaccard overlap 0.505. Adding symmetric electrical edges at the primary threshold gave deficits of zero and five. Thus one maximum matching hides broad target choice, and graph rules change that choice. We preserve an exact classification tool, graph edges, ranks, source hashes and independent checks. These are structural-rank results for selected finite graphs. They do not establish biological control, input accessibility, dynamics or behavior. The graphs omit intrinsic dynamics and use independent-entry assumptions that need not hold for electrical coupling.

display.caption: A small chemical matching deficit permits almost all neurons as unmatched targets. Edge thresholds and electrical edges change the possible set. These are graph results, not measured control.

citations.reason: Its electrical-edge import rule informed this graph audit. No code or tables were reused.
